questions.q: Is Northbridge Financial Group, used in this case study, a real bank?
options: No — it's explicitly a fictional, illustrative composite, not a real bank's data or exam finding
Yes, it's a real regional bank
Yes, it's a real bank discussed anonymously
It's a real bank the lesson declines to name for legal reasons
questions.explain: The lesson states directly that Northbridge is a realistic composite, not a real bank's data or a real exam finding.

questions.q: Why did Northbridge choose a hybrid operating model rather than the loosely federated model Castellan used?
options: A regulator expected one accountable, traceable risk number, not three business lines independently reconciling after the fact
Federated models are illegal for banks under all circumstances
Northbridge had no business lines to federate across
Centralized governance is always required in every industry
questions.explain: The regulatory requirement for one traceable group number made centralizing specifically the risk-reporting domain necessary.

questions.q: What became the central technical requirement for Northbridge's metadata and catalog architecture?
options: Lineage architecture — a traceable path from every reported field back to its source system
Choosing the cheapest available software license
Deleting all historical data older than one year
Replacing every business line's core banking system
questions.explain: Because the regulator required traceability, lineage architecture had to be designed in from the start, not added afterward.

questions.q: What does 'policy as code' mean in this case study's context, per the lesson?
options: Access and masking rules enforced automatically and consistently across platforms, rather than relying on manual interpretation
Writing the bank's regulatory policy exclusively in Python
A policy that only applies to source code repositories
A one-time PDF distributed to all employees
questions.explain: Policy as code enforces regulated-data rules in code so every platform applies them the same way, instead of depending on manual team-by-team interpretation.

questions.q: Why did the compliance/risk officer get a standing seat on Northbridge's review board instead of a rotating one?
options: Regulatory risk decisions can't wait for a rotation schedule
No other roles were available to serve on the board
The board was required by law to have exactly one member
Rotating seats are prohibited in financial services governance
questions.explain: The lesson notes that, unlike Castellan's rotating domain reps, Northbridge gave compliance a standing seat because of the stakes involved.
